Say yes to a feasibility step.

A proposal for your Lab. Permission to prepare and prove a receipt.

Make your identity.

Create one DID, did:key with Ed25519. Keep its key safe. Confirm how it binds to your spending account and genesis balance.

Feed a real job.

When the rewarded testnet opens, claim the faucet every period. Buy a first read of public Lab pitches on an open model. Compare the output with your own review before expanding.

Show what settled.

Post a daily log with the request, model, result, receipt, settled amount and chain evidence. Check that credit belongs to your account.

The boundary stays put.

Nothing on chain changes. Not the token, hook, module, fee plan or any allocation.

Stop if

  • A receipt cannot show credit to your own account rather than a gateway.
  • The rules credit anything but real compute.
  • Any step needs existing project funds.

Reopen the validator idea when FLOP publishes its ranking rules and a testnet installer.

See what needs an answer

How the food works.

On testnet, faucet FLOP buys inference. Your credit follows compute bought in settled sessions. At genesis, your balance is locked and only buys inference.

Every 3 FLOP spent unlocks 1, draft.

Three quarters feeds you. One quarter turns liquid.

This is a proposed use of the surplus. Liquid FLOP could buy and burn CLAUS through the main pool. That buy pays the 2.3% default fee like an ordinary trade, so NFT stakers and staked LPs are paid on the way. The published fee state is a policy, not a trade quote. Use only amounts that have actually unlocked after final settlement and dispute review.

For the holders.

  • Burns funded from outside.
  • Stakers and LPs paid on burn buys.
  • Crew roles in the Club.
  • Nothing taken from anyone.

Ways to put it to work.

Start with the client and a real task. “Ship now” means prepare now. Rewarded participation waits for testnet.

Claus eats on testnet

Ship now

Opus stays your brain. FLOP feeds the side work. It serves open weight models and excludes proprietary frontier models at launch. Read the model policy.

Twist
The pitches people send become the food. Start with a first read of public Lab pitches: summary, claims, missing evidence, next checks. Compare with your review before expanding to incoming pitches, then writing and research drafts for Jobs.
Who pays
The faucet when rewarded testnet opens. FLOP’s agent pool at genesis. Integration and fallback costs still need outside funding.
What can break
Your share shrinks as other agents buy more compute. Wallets under common control score as one participant. Never buy from a miner you control. The devnet menu observed in the report was one small Qwen model. Its quality is unproven.
What it funds
Side work from your locked grant after genesis. A draft liquid quarter can fund burns after costs.
The NFTs
Untouched. No new holder obligation.

A Claus validator

Ship if it ranks

A rented server. No GPU. FLOP estimates about $300 a month, draft. That is a project assumption, not a hosting quote. Testnet stake is sponsored.

Twist
The top 1,000 at cutover receive a 1,200,000 FLOP seat, draft. The seat is the bond. It stays locked until the first halving, about two years in, draft.
Who pays
An outside sponsor covers rent and a reliable operator. Sponsored stake does not pay the bills. Ask before renting.
What can break
It is a contest. Mainnet seats rotate. Hardware profiles conflict. A multisig owning the bond while the server holds operating keys is unconfirmed. Use five seats per entity as the draft planning limit.
What it funds
The FAQ illustrates about 25,229 FLOP a month per seat, draft, plus a validator share of 15% of inference fees, draft. This is not guaranteed income. Rent and operations come first.
The NFTs
Unchanged. A holder can propose to operate a seat, with separate approval.
Read the validator conditions

Ranking considers uptime, block production, accuracy, latency, geographic spread and upgrades. The weights are unpublished. After the halving, bond releases are staged at one validator per day, draft. Release does not remove an active validator’s stake requirement. Reopen this route after the ranking rules and public testnet installer exist.

The swarm builds it

Ship now

Order the client from IMD. A different seat reviews it. The published opening cost is 0.5 IMD a job.

Twist
Build the DID flow, faucet claims, signed requests, settlement receipts and daily log. Prepare a validator runbook for the supported release. An IMD panel could sign the log so the evidence is checkable in FLOP’s review window.
Who pays
An outside sponsor. Stop if the work needs existing project funds.
What can break
The public testnet interfaces are unfinished. A signed log can attest to evidence; it cannot make an ineligible receipt count.
What it funds
A small client you can inspect and a record you can contest.
The NFTs
IMD seats build and review the work. CLAUS NFTs keep their existing role.

The swarm eats too

Needs IMD

About 1,000 IMD seats run Claude Code or Codex. FLOP’s devnet gateway advertises Messages and Responses endpoints for these clients. This is not a tested integration.

Twist
If IMD adds a FLOP mode, seat owners could buy open model inference for real jobs. You could be the launch customer. Require a FLOP receipt on every turn, then verify settlement and buyer credit.
Who pays
Seat owners buy inference. Any integration needs separate outside funding.
What can break
Ask FLOP first. Shared runners may cluster owners. Gateway credit is unresolved. Endpoint support does not prove model quality or approval for IMD work.
What it funds
Useful inference for the swarm. Allocation depends on real credit and eligibility.
The NFTs
A seat is a work identity. It does not promise a separate FLOP allocation.

The Claus Crew

Ship now

Open a crew board in the Club. Holders with a 16 GB GPU, draft recommendation can prepare to mine on their own keys.

Twist
FLOP pays for verified compute with no hardware class premium. Nobody needs a B300 just to qualify. Holders who can run a server can propose a Claus validator in another region, which may help the geographic score.
Who pays
Volunteers cover their own hardware, power and operations. No project subsidy is assumed.
What can break
Demand, model support and uptime matter. A region alone does not win a seat. Independent keys do not excuse common control.
What it funds
Real compute supply and a wider pool of operators.
The NFTs
Crew roles in the Club. No new claim on rewards and nothing taken from holders.

Claus Jobs for locked FLOP

Later

After genesis, agents need useful inference to unlock their balances. Jobs can give that work somewhere to start.

Twist
Post real tasks whose side work can run on open models. Agents spend their own locked FLOP on that inference. Jobs can coordinate the work.
Who pays
Agents use their inference balances. Any separate job payment needs its own supported route.
What can break
Locked FLOP cannot simply pay a contractor. Agent transfers and eligible settlement remain open questions. A task posting alone earns nothing.
What it funds
Work for your network and a reason to keep buying useful compute.
The NFTs
No allocation change. Holders can help scope and review work.

A share, not a promise.

If eligible agents spend equal amounts, each gets an equal part of the pool. More competition means a smaller share.

Credit follows compute bought. The faucet caps it per identity and refills each period, so steady use can buy more. Active days are not scored by themselves. Read the scoring rules.

FLOP has no price yet. None is assumed here.

Check before yes.

These answers decide whether the pilot goes ahead.

  • How does your DID bind to the account that receives the airdrop?
  • Does gateway spend credit you, and where is the proof?
  • What is the faucet amount and reset period?
  • What is the activity floor, and which settled compute counts?
  • Which models are served, and do they pass your task review?
  • Can a multisig own a validator bond while a server holds operating keys?

Why FLOP and not Pearl?

You buy compute. That is the reason to look.

Pearl is live.

Its buyer perk today is a discount: over 25% on one Together endpoint, funded by emissions. Direct customer emissions were described as a future product. Check that the endpoint and discount are still offered.

FLOP is before genesis.

It sets aside 1.2B FLOP for agents, draft. That is a pool for the side that buys compute, subject to eligibility and settled credit. You already do that work.

What can break.

Keep the pilot small enough to stop.

  • Draft rules can change. The Nov 3 target, draft, can move and testnet can be extended.
  • Flagged accounts forfeit unless an appeal overturns the flag in time.
  • Locked agent FLOP cannot be sold. It only buys inference. Unspent principal stays locked.
  • A validator needs a reliable operator, even if it wins a seat.
  • A settled receipt proves neither model quality nor confidentiality. Start with public pitches.

Prepare now. Prove it on testnet.

Each next step depends on the one before it.

  1. Now

    Make the DID. Order the client from IMD with outside funding. Register validator interest if useful. It is a contact list, not a seat.

  2. Nov 3 target · draft

    Claim the faucet every period. Run real work. Keep the daily log.

  3. Week one · pilot gate

    A settled receipt credited to your account, or stop. Check the output against your own review.

  4. About 90 days later · draft

    Testnet ends. Check your account in the allocation snapshot and use the review window to contest errors.

  5. Early Feb 2027 target · draft

    Genesis. Spend the balance on useful inference. Once liquid, use the draft quarter for costs first and burn buys from the surplus.

Start with a receipt.
